# Was the Workday outage a hack?

**Not established.** Not established. Workday says it was not a cyber incident and describes a fault in its own disaster-recovery setup. No independent source confirms that, and Workday has published no root-cause report.

Incident: Workday HR and payroll outage, Nov 13-14, 2026. Also reported as the Workday outage and the Workday payroll outage. First published Nov 20, 2026; last updated Nov 20, 2026, 6:55 PM ET.

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Workday, any government agency, news outlet, company, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 20, 2026, 6:55 PM ET: **Axios reports that suspected bots wrote about a third of the conspiracy posts during the Workday outage; the cause is unchanged.** Added s017, a Nov 19 Axios report (Tier 2) citing PeakMetrics data: suspected bots accounted for 34% of conspiracy-related posts during the Workday outage, versus 27% of other posts, and Axios says there is no publicly established evidence of a coordinated cyberattack. Added c011 as Reported (one outlet relaying one firm's analysis) and linked it to q002. No label change on q001, which stays Not established. Checked, not found: a Workday root-cause report, an SEC 8-K about the outage (latest 8-K Oct 23), a CISA or regulator statement naming Workday. Staleness check done on the head. Privacy check done: no reporter names, handles or usernames.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Large. Workday serves about 11,500 organizations and is a service many employees rely on for pay, time and benefits. The outage lasted about a day for most customers. Nobody has said how many organizations or people were affected.
- Who is affected: Employees at organizations that use Workday, who could not clock in, see pay, request time off or file for benefits from the afternoon of Nov 13 until Nov 14. Service is back for most customers. Check your employer's notice for any benefits deadline or timecard steps.

| Value | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| Nov 13 | Outage began | Friday afternoon, ET |
| 11 AM Sat | Service restored, per Workday | Some customers returned later |
| 11,500 | Organizations Workday serves | Total customers, not the number affected |

### Known so far

- Workday's customer notice said its disaster-recovery site unexpectedly connected to production databases. This is what Workday said, not an independent finding.
- Workday said the outage was not related to a cybersecurity incident. This is the company's own statement, not an independent finding.
- Workday acknowledged a service disruption on Friday, Nov 13.
- Employees at affected organizations could not clock in, see pay, request time off or file for benefits.
- Workday said service was restored by 11 AM ET on Saturday, Nov 14. Some employers reported restoration at other times.
- A Nov 18 White House release says officials see no indication of a coordinated cyberattack behind recent tech outages. It does not name Workday.

### Not known yet

- Whether the outage was a cyberattack. Workday says it was not; no independent source has confirmed that.
- The root cause. Workday has not published a report or said how its disaster-recovery services reached production databases.
- How many customers and employees were affected. Workday has not said.
- Whether any customer data was lost or changed. Employers told staff to check their own records and pending requests.
- Whether a regulator, CISA or an outside investigator will say anything about it. None had at the last check.

## What Workday and others said

> Some of our customers are experiencing a service disruption and we're working urgently to investigate and resolve the issue. We sincerely apologize for the challenges this is causing impacted customers.
>
> — Workday statement to KRON4, Nov 13

> While validating the weekly Maintenance Window for Disaster Recovery tenants, we have identified that tenanted services within the DR Site unexpectedly connected to Production databases. As a result, this has left data in an inconsistent state that can cause errors accessing tenants or jobs/integrations/tasks to fail with missing transaction error messages. Effective immediately, we are placing all WD1 Production tenants into Maintenance while our teams investigate the best recovery path.
>
> — Workday notice on its Community Status Page, as quoted by Washington University in St. Louis IT, Nov 13

> Workday said Saturday that a widespread outage of its human resources platform was not related to a cybersecurity incident.
>
> — WUSA9, Nov 14, reporting a Workday spokesperson's statement

## What we checked and did not find

- A Workday root-cause or post-incident report. Not found as of Nov 20, 11:00 AM ET.
- An SEC filing from Workday about the outage. Not found.
- A CISA, FBI or other government statement naming Workday. Not found. The Nov 18 White House release covers other outages and does not mention Workday.
- Any credible claim of a hack, breach, ransomware or data theft at Workday. Not found. The only claim of a different cause timeline comes from forum posts repeated by a vendor blog (c010).
- A public Workday status page. Workday's own pages were not logged into; recaps say customer updates reached the public through employers' status pages.
- A Workday post on X. Not checked.
- The San Francisco Chronicle original. Not read directly; its reporting is cited through other outlets.
